title: The L2 Fourier isometry and its Schwartz-test identity
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure on $\mathbf R^m$, $m\geq1$. Let $L^2$ be measurable complex functions with finite $\int|u|^2$, modulo almost-everywhere equality, with norm $(\int|u|^2)^{1/2}$. Let $\mathcal S$ consist of smooth complex functions $\phi$ with $\sup_x\|x\|^k\|D^n\phi(x)\|<\infty$ for all integers $k,n\geq0$, and set $\mathcal F\phi(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\phi(x)\,dx$. There is a complex-linear isometric bijection $\mathcal F_2:L^2\to L^2$ whose value on the class of each $\phi\in\mathcal S$ is the class of $\mathcal F\phi$. For every $u\in L^2$, every measurable representative $u_0$ of $u$, every measurable representative $w_0$ of $\mathcal F_2u$, and every $\phi\in\mathcal S$, one has $$\int\phi(\xi)w_0(\xi)\,d\xi=\int(\mathcal F\phi)(x)u_0(x)\,dx.$$
